topic: The 1987 Black Monday crash: triggers and market recovery

script.title: 1987 Black Monday crash triggers and market recovery explained
script.hook: What caused Black Monday to wipe out trillions overnight?

scenes.text: What caused Black Monday to wipe out trillions overnight?

motion_action.headline: What caused Black Monday to wipe out

scenes.text: On October fifth, 1987, the Dow fell about twenty‑two percent.

motion_action.result_headline: Dow fell about twenty‑two percent on Oct 5, 1987

scenes.text: Program trading algorithms amplified the sell‑off in seconds.
Portfolio insurers tried to hedge, but triggered cascading stops.
About one trillion dollars vanished in market value that day.
The crash spread globally, causing markets worldwide to tumble.
Many believe circuit breakers stop crashes completely.
In reality they only pause trading, giving markets time to breathe.

motion_action.statement: They only pause trading, giving markets time to breathe

scenes.text: Within two years, the Dow recovered to pre‑crash levels, proving resilience.

script.description:
What caused Black Monday to wipe out trillions overnight? Learn the triggers behind the 1987 crash and how markets bounced back. Explore algorithmic trading, portfolio insurance, and circuit breakers.

#Shorts #money #economics #finance
script.comment_question: Which trigger mattered most: algorithmic trading or portfolio insurance?
review_notes: FIXED: Scene 2: "On October fifth, 1987, the Dow plunged 22 point percent." (The phrasing “22 point percent” is nonsensical; the Dow fell 22 percent, not 22 point percent.)
FIXED: Scene 5: "Over 1.5 trillion dollars vanished in market value that day." (The actual market value loss on Black Monday was closer to 1 trillion dollars, not 1.5 trillion.)

FIXED: Scene 6: "The crash spread globally, wiping out 23 percent of US equity value." (There is no evidence the US equity market lost 23 % of its value globally on that day; the drop was about 22 % in the Dow, not a global 23 %)
